edges.description: Failed or incomplete prosencephalon division is the core forebrain-patterning phenotype.
Forebrain midline-patterning disruption impairs telencephalic commissure formation, causing corpus callosum agenesis.
Midline prosencephalic cleavage failure disrupts formation of the septum pellucidum.
Impaired FGFR1-dependent olfactory placode and forebrain development causes absence of olfactory bulbs and tracts.
Midline central nervous system developmental disruption extends to cerebellar vermian hypoplasia.
Holoprosencephaly-spectrum cortical and midline malformation predisposes to medically refractory epilepsy.
Structural forebrain malformation impairs upper motor neuron pathways, producing spasticity.
Forebrain malformation and associated neurologic dysfunction cause global developmental delay.
Midline hypothalamic developmental dysfunction impairs central thermoregulation.
Midline hypothalamic developmental dysfunction disrupts circadian sleep-wake regulation.
Neurologic and oromotor dysfunction from forebrain malformation and craniofacial clefting cause feeding difficulties.
Defective FGFR1-dependent hypothalamic GnRH neuron development causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
Midline hypothalamic-posterior pituitary developmental dysfunction causes central diabetes insipidus.
Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, feeding impairment, and FGFR1 developmental signaling deficiency contribute to postnatal growth retardation.
Fetal gonadotropin deficiency secondary to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism leads to micropenis in affected males.
Deficient hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis signaling impairs testicular descent, causing cryptorchidism.
Rostral midline prosencephalic and frontonasal patterning disruption causes cleft lip.
Midline craniofacial patterning disruption causes palatal clefting.
Incomplete midline frontonasal and eye-field separation within the holoprosencephaly spectrum causes hypotelorism in a subset of patients.
Variable frontonasal craniofacial dysmorphism in FGFR1-related Hartsfield syndrome occasionally manifests with ocular hypertelorism.
Impaired limb-bud patterning disrupts central-ray formation across hands and feet, producing ectrodactyly.
Disrupted anteroposterior autopod ray specification in FGFR1 deficiency occasionally produces supernumerary or bifid digits.
Impaired interdigital separation and ray patterning in the developing autopod produce cutaneous or osseous syndactyly.

evidence.reference_title: Malformation Pattern and Molecular Findings in the FGFR1-Related Hartsfield Syndrome Phenotype
evidence.snippet: The malformation phenotype of HRTFDS has been reviewed in 26 previously reported patients in terms of single congenital defects, mutational spectrum, impacted protein domains and inheritance. Molecular basis, clinical management, main differential diagnoses and genetic counseling were also illustrated. Results: SHFM was identified in every patient.

The diagnosis of FGFR1-related Hartsfield syndrome is established in a proband with suggestive findings and either an FGFR1 heterozygous pathogenic variant (in those with autosomal dominant inheritance) or FGFR1 biallelic pathogenic variants (in those with autosomal recessive inheritance) identified by molecular genetic testing.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants clustering in the ATP-binding and catalytic pocket of the FGFR1 intracellular tyrosine kinase domain create receptor subunits that form inactive dimers with wild-type FGFR1, exerting a dominant-negative blockade on receptor transphosphorylation and downstream FGF-stimulated RAS/ERK1/2 signaling and c-Fos induction. Rarely, homozygous missense variants in the extracellular Ig-like ligand-binding domain D2 abolish FGF ligand binding and phenocopy severe FGFR1 signaling loss.

nodes.description: Loss of FGFR1 signaling in the rostral prosencephalon and anterior neural ridge during early embryogenesis impairs midline cleavage of the embryonic forebrain and development of commissural, olfactory placode, and hypothalamic-pituitary structures. This produces the holoprosencephaly spectrum (alobar, semilobar, or lobar), corpus callosum agenesis, absent septum pellucidum, arrhinencephaly, cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, midline craniofacial clefting and variable orbital spacing, neurologic dysfunction (including hypothalamic thermoregulatory and sleep-wake disturbances), postnatal growth retardation, and hypothalamic-pituitary endocrinopathies.

evidence.snippet: HPE spectrum disorder, resulting from failed or incomplete forebrain division early in gestation, includes alobar, semilobar, or lobar HPE. Other observed midline brain malformations include corpus callosum agenesis, absent septum pellucidum, absent olfactory bulbs and tracts, and vermian hypoplasia.
